$comment: What OPCUA_RECONNECT_MAX_RETRY may be, and what one connection round then does, driven through BOTH runtimes: tests/unit/test_reconnect.py and packages/server-node/test/reconnect.test.mjs read this file and assert the same verdict, the same sentence and the same round (#136). `maxRetry` is the parsed value, or `error` is the exact message the setting is refused with. `delays` is the backoff of one round in ms — its length is how many retries that round makes, which on the Node runtime is what node-opcua is handed. -1 means no round is ever the last, not that one round never ends: an unbounded round is a request that never returns, which is what a Node server started against an unreachable endpoint was, from `initialize` onwards. Every case uses initialDelay 1000 and maxDelay 8000, the defaults.
